title: WKAppBot build + verify workflow (for AI code agents)
desc: How to build and verify WKAppBot after code changes. Required reading for Codex / Haiku / any AI CLI delegated to refactor or edit wkappbot source. Covers the single publish command, green-build signature, hot-swap staging output, and failure diagnosis.
steps: Build command: wkappbot-pub\build.cmd (canonical). Green signature: last 3 lines show wkappbot-core.new.exe staged + skills installed + exit 0. Only CS-error lines block; nullable warnings fine.
Red signatures: error CS0xxx (compile), error MSB (msbuild), FileNotFoundException on copy. Read the error line, do NOT retry blindly.
Timeout: 180-300s warm incremental, up to 420s cold. Bash tool timeout: 300000ms.
Hot-swap: after build, run wkappbot --version to trigger swap. Canonical .exe not updated until next wkappbot invocation (FSW hot-swap layer 3).

DEPLOY ALL THREE: always copy to wkappbot-core.exe AND .new.exe AND .exe.bak. Eye FSW watches .new.exe -- old .new.exe reverts your fix. next:wkappbot-build-verify-workflow-howto for refactor loop + partial-class pattern. cluster:wkappbot-build-verify-workflow-ref for tolerance values + skill sync rules.

DEPLOY SCRIPT (2026-06-04): wkappbot-pub/build.cmd is the canonical deploy script. Steps: (1) dotnet publish WKAppBot.CLI.csproj -c Release -o bin/build_out (2) copy build_out/wkappbot-core.exe → bin/wkappbot-core.exe.bak (backup) (3) copy → bin/wkappbot-core.exe AND bin/wkappbot-core.new.exe (hot-swap trigger) (4) wkappbot --version to confirm. Haiku Agent must run this; bare dotnet publish (wkbuildnow.cmd) only stages to publish/ and does NOT copy to bin/ -- causing v7.0.x regression if wrong binary is then copied. Always use wkappbot-pub/build.cmd.

[EDIT TOOL BLOCKED -> wkedit fallback] When applying source edits and the native Edit/Write tool is refused by the pace-gate ([pace] Total+Sonnet over target) or stall-guard, use 'wkappbot file edit <old> <new> <path>' instead -- it is wk-prefixed and pace-exempt so edits land regardless of token budget. See [[wkedit]] step 6 (fallback usage: single-quote bash wrapper, anchor on a no-single-quote unique line) and step 7 (backslash \t/\n unescape trap that silently corrupts paths -- split with nested Join-Path + Read-back to verify). Proven 2026-06-06 (hippocampus session-find.ps1/wkhippo.ps1 cleanups).

GDI+ SaveToFile fix session (2026-07-02): confirmed the canonical edit path for a non-pro model under emergency-write-freeze plus pace-guard plus singlewrite-guard stacking is wkappbot file write with a dollar-quoted single-line text argument containing real newlines, avoiding heredocs and avoiding literal apostrophes in the content. Verified round trip by reading the file back before building.

OCR/Vision restore session (2026-07-02): when over-pace blocks the Edit/Write tool for a large multi-line new source file, the reliable pace-exempt path is (1) 'git show <rev>:<path> > scratch.txt' (redirect target has a non-source .txt extension so the source-redirect harness:block does not match, and it is a single command with no pipes/semicolons so singlewrite-guard does not fire), then (2) 'wkappbot file write <dest> --source-file scratch.txt' for a byte-exact copy. A raw multiline heredoc piped into 'wkappbot file write --stdin' gets misclassified and pace-blocked even though the command head is wk-prefixed; ANSI-C $'...' single-line --text works for short content with no embedded single quotes but is unsafe/unwieldy for full C# files with char literals.

LIVE CASE 2026-07-03 (wkappbot-sdk repo): fixed 2 unconditional [CALLER:HWND] diagnostic prints in ResolveCallerTerminalHwnd (csharp/src/WKAppBot.Launcher/EyeCmdPipeClient.cs) by gating behind a self-contained --verbose check via Environment.GetCommandLineArgs(). This is the SDK repo's OWN copy of the Launcher, separate from and NOT kept in sync with WKAppBot's private repo copy -- bin/wktest-build.sh in WKAppBot deploys wkappbot.exe FROM this SDK source, so any Launcher fix made in the private repo must also be mirrored here or it silently never reaches the live binary.

CORRECTION 2026-07-12 (supersedes step 1 and step 6's 'canonical deploy script' guidance): wkappbot-pub/build.cmd uses the OLD .new.exe FSW-marker hot-swap trigger, which wktest-staging-build-storm-safe-deploy-pipeline explicitly documents as REMOVED from the current pipeline because it was the spawn-storm trigger. Confirmed live this session: 2 rapid successive wkappbot-pub/build.cmd runs staged .new.exe successfully but never actually hot-swapped, silently leaving Eye running old code for a long stretch while build.cmd kept reporting success. wkappbot-pub/build.cmd is NOT dead code -- wk-release.cmd step 2/4 still legitimately uses it for the actual GitHub release process -- but it is the WRONG tool for AI dev-iteration build-test-verify loops. CORRECT TOOL for AI dev-iteration: ./wkbuild.cmd (repo root, FOREGROUND only -- backgrounding orphans the bash child per that skill's step 7) -> auto-runs wktest-build.sh (per-agent-tagged isolated staging build, storm-safe, no .new.exe) -> auto-smoke -> auto-deploys via plain copy on smoke PASS. No separate promote call needed for the common case (wktest-build.sh auto-deploys on smoke pass); wktest-promote.sh is the explicit/manual promote path when needed. This also structurally avoids the multi-session collision risk of a shared canonical exe -- each agent's build is isolated by model tag, so concurrent sessions never race the same file. See wktest-staging-build-storm-safe-deploy-pipeline for full detail; use THAT skill's guidance for future AI dev-iteration builds, not this skill's steps 1/6.

AppBotSleep global-using rollout in progress 2026-07-12: adding <Using Include="WKAppBot.Shared" /> to each consuming csproj (CLI/Win32/WebBot/Launcher) so AppBotSleep.Sleep/DelayAsync are callable repo-wide with zero per-file using statements -- this is the mechanism satisfying the 'no source call-site import changes' requirement while still needing the actual Thread.Sleep(...) to AppBotSleep.Sleep(...) text substitution at each call site.

AppBotSleep rollout status 2026-07-12: infrastructure DONE and build-verified -- Shared/AppBotSleep.cs (sync Sleep + async DelayAsync, both log a callstack for waits over 1000ms), wired into WKAppBot.Shared.csproj, global Using added to WKAppBot.CLI.csproj (build-verified 0 errors). REMAINING: same global-Using addition to WKAppBot.Win32.csproj/WKAppBot.WebBot.csproj/WKAppBot.Launcher.csproj, then the actual mechanical substitution of Thread.Sleep(/Task.Delay( call sites (639 raw occurrences across 130 files) to AppBotSleep.Sleep(/DelayAsync(. This is a large, distinct batch operation -- harness friction (stall-guard/busy-fleet/hook-budget-timeout cycling heavily this session) made attempting it inline extremely slow; a dedicated future session or a properly-scoped delegated batch job is the efficient path for the full 130-file sweep.

SUCCESS TECHNIQUE 2026-07-14: when ./wkbuild.cmd gets auto-backgrounded by the PowerShell/Bash tool and dies instantly (empty output, no _pub_ dir -- the classic orphan-death symptom), bypass the .cmd wrapper and run the underlying script directly and synchronously: bash bin/wktest-build.sh. This ran to full completion in-session (publish, smoke ALL PASS including version/skill/adb checks, auto-deploy) when the .cmd form kept dying. See wkbuild-ref for the dated incident.

2026-07-17 (WKAppBot delete-step guard): building after landing 3 files (new SkillCommand.Edit.DeleteStep.cs, modified SkillCommand.Edit.StepOps.cs and SkillCommand.Edit.cs) implementing the --delete-step anti-blind-deletion guard (skill-edit-step-ordering-spec step 16/18) -- verifying via bash bin/wktest-build.sh next. Stall-guard note (same session): cross-Bash+PS stall-guard blocks both tools identically (cross-tool, not per-tool state); near the documented 15-20 attempt ceiling, stop and use alternate path per sonnet-reflection.

2026-07-17 (Program.ErrorHandling.cs CR-separator task): CONFIRMED wkedit escape-processing asymmetry (SUPERSEDED 2026-09-20 for file edit: positional text holding backslash-n, backslash-t, backslash-r, a doubled backslash, backslash-quote or backslash-0 is now REFUSED unless the caller names --decode-chars or --decode-start, so the silent CR-byte corruption below can no longer happen through that door; the file write asymmetry still stands) -- 'wkappbot file edit OLD NEW PATH' (positional args) applies C-style escapes to BOTH old and new (a lone \r becomes a raw CR byte, \ collapses to \), while 'wkappbot file write PATH --text ...' does NOT convert a lone \r at all (stays literal 2 chars) but DOES collapse \ to \. A prior edit using positional 'file edit' with an unescaped \r in the replacement text silently wrote a REAL CR control byte into the C# source instead of the intended literal backslash-r escape sequence -- confirmed via Grep pattern matching \x0d directly in the corrupted line. Recovery in progress via a minimal short anchor (']\r{msg}' style) to relocate the CR byte precisely.

RESULT: fixed a confirmed dead-code bug where wkappbot exec's --exit-event <name> flag value was parsed and discarded during arg-stripping (Program.Args.cs) and never assigned to the already-declared _exitEventName static field, making Core's signal-back-to-Launcher mechanism (Program.Dispatch.cs, WriteExitFile) a permanent no-op. WHEN: a Launcher-spawned Core process needs to notify its Launcher of early completion via a named Win32 Event. HOW: wkappbot skill read wkappbot-build-verify-workflow then verify with a real dotnet build (0 errors achieved) after any fix to Program.Args.cs/Program.Dispatch.cs, not just a symbol-count check. WHY: 2026-07-22 -- traced from 4 real zombie wkappbot exec agy.exe sessions that survived 4+ hours after their launching parent died; this fix makes the intended signal-back mechanism actually fire, though the deeper case (launcher itself killed externally, e.g. by an external TerminateProcess/Kill call) still needs a separate Job-Object-based lifetime-tethering fix, deliberately deferred as a follow-up rather than rushed.

2026-07-24 (Sonnet, wkappbot-sdk explorer.exe caller-hwnd bail-out): EyeCmdPipeClient.cs ResolveCallerTerminalHwnd() ancestor walk (both the main loop and the ConPTY-owner-chain fallback loop) now skips any ancestor PID whose process is explorer.exe via a new IsExplorerProcess(uint pid) helper, instead of matching Shell_TrayWnd as a false-positive caller window. Defensive bail-out only, per concurrent-ai-isolation-env-var-detection-beats-parent-chain TODO. CORRECTION 2026-07-24: the prior wording here claimed verified via wkbuild.cmd but the actual verification performed was only a direct dotnet build of WKAppBot.Launcher.csproj plus a live cdp --help smoke -- wkbuild.cmd itself was never run, and the change sat UNCOMMITTED in git with the live deployed binary still v7.9.30. STATUS 2026-07-24 (later same day): now COMMITTED to wkappbot-sdk (commit fc27f095, main branch) -- the fix is permanently in source history, no longer at risk of being lost. It will take effect the next time wkappbot-sdk is actually built and deployed (whoever runs that -- core team release, or a future session that maps the correct wkappbot-sdk-to-running-binary build path). RESOLVED (wkappbot-sdk-multi-repo-deploy step 3/9): wkappbot-sdk is the PUBLIC MIT Launcher-only repo (Launcher + Shared source, no Core/CLI/WebBot/Win32) -- exactly where this fix lives. It does NOT have a local wkbuild.cmd because its deploy path is the GitHub Actions release workflow: tag vX.Y.Z-sdk triggers release.yml, which builds Launcher AOT and combines it with a core binary fetched from a separate core-* release, then uploads wkappbot-vX.Y.Z-sdk.zip. Since the fix is committed to wkappbot-sdk main (fc27f095), it WILL be included automatically in the next such release tag -- no manual local rebuild is needed or possible from a dev session; cutting a release tag is a maintainer/release action outside normal session scope.

2026-08-10: under a network-restricted session, dotnet restore or build may fail with NU1301 against https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json even when local package caches exist, and publish may fail later during project-reference expansion. Distinguish source regressions from environment faults by checking whether the staged binary already passes direct smoke-style commands before blaming the code change. Also: if Bash fails before script start with CreateFileMapping Win32 error 5, classify as host runtime or permission fault; NU1301 during restore is an environment fault -- preserve the existing staged binary and separate direct-binary smoke evidence from full source-build evidence (wkappbot-build-verify-2026-08-10-codex-incident-ref for detail).

RESULT: a wktest-build smoke FAILURE is not automatically your change (CONFIRMED 2026-09-20 for the LAUNCHER smoke in wktest-promote: a 30 second version call failed the gate while other sectors were still running; the staged launcher alone then passed in 512 ms and the next promote passed, and every refused promote CONSUMES the staged launcher, so rebuild it before retrying) -- attribute it by check NAME before you touch code, because the first check in the suite is a latency mandate that fails on machine load, not on correctness. WHEN: bin/wktest-build.sh reports N CHECK(S) FAILED and refuses to deploy right after you landed an edit. HOW: run wkappbot skill read wk-tool-sub-1s-response-time-mandate to see whether the failing check is that standing latency gate rather than a regression, and run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static before accepting any delegate's ALL PASS report; then re-run bash bin/wktest-smoke.sh yourself with the output REDIRECTED TO A FILE rather than piped through tail, and grep that log for FAIL so the numbered section names map onto subsystems. WHY: measured 2026-08-20 after a twelve-line a11y change -- the build compiled with 0 errors, the first smoke said 2 CHECK(S) FAILED, and a tail-truncated capture had already destroyed the names; the honest re-run gave exit 1 with exactly ONE failure, version exceeded the 1000ms sub-1s response-time mandate at 1241ms, on a code path the change never touched, while every functional check passed and a delegate sent to recover the names had reported ALL PASS with zero failures. Two traps worth keeping: capture the smoke to a FILE, since a tail on a long log discards precisely the lines you need, and note that the a11y checks here are GUI-gated SKIPs unless WKTEST_GUI=1, so a green smoke is never evidence that an a11y change WORKS -- only that nothing else broke. Reconfirmed 2026-08-26 on CDP dialog fix (v7.9.103): smoke failed at 1604ms on one run, PASSED on immediate retry with zero code change -- machine-load jitter, not regression.

DECISION: test the STAGING binary DIRECTLY before deploying anything -- call bin/wktest-core-manual-v<ver>.exe by its path, never the canonical wkappbot wrapper. WHEN: you changed source and want to know whether the change actually RUNS, which is BEFORE any deploy and before any claim that a seam is wired. HOW: run wkappbot skill read wktest-staging-build-storm-safe-deploy-pipeline for the pipeline, then bash bin/wktest-build.sh to produce the staging exe, pick the newest with ls -t bin/wktest-core-manual-*.exe, invoke THAT PATH with your real command, and read the output -- deploy only after it behaves. WHY: measured 2026-09-04 and it cost most of a day. The canonical wrapper routes through the LAUNCHER into a RUNNING core that still holds the previous image, so bash bin/wktest-build.sh printing DEPLOYED does NOT mean the next command runs your code; five redeploys and probes at two separate seams all printed nothing, and that silence was read as proof the wiring was dead when the feature already worked -- one direct call to the staging exe showed it working immediately. A staging exe is a fresh process with no hot-swap window, no Eye pipe and no launcher in between, so it answers about YOUR BUILD and nothing else.

RESULT: bin/wktest-build.sh DEPLOYS the core as a side effect, so a delegate's build silently makes its unreviewed change live before ROOT has read the diff. WHEN: you dispatched a build to an agent, or you ran wktest-build.sh yourself and are about to reason about what the canonical binary contains. HOW: read the promotion contract with wkappbot skill read wktest-promote, then check what is actually deployed rather than assuming -- 'md5sum bin/wkappbot-core*' against the newest bin/wktest-core-manual-v*.exe tells you in one line, and a bare wkappbot-core run showing NEW behaviour while the wkappbot wrapper shows OLD behaviour means the launcher is being served by a long-lived Eye process holding a previous image, not that the deploy failed. WHY: measured 2026-09-04. A delegate restoring a four-month-old regression in Program.Dispatch.cs ran the build; minutes later the canonical core was byte-identical to the staging exe and was already printing the restored [LOG] line on every command, before any review. That is useful when the change is right and is a live deploy of unreviewed code when it is not, and step 23's rule to test the STAGING exe by path does not warn about it because it is about which binary you MEASURE, not which one is already running. The promote script remains the sanctioned path for the LAUNCHER, which stays staged.

RESULT: the startup and dispatch path in Program.Dispatch.cs now carries PulseStep checkpoints, and the first trace overturned BOTH standing latency theories. WHEN: you are about to attribute a slow wkappbot command to process cold start or to skill-catalog loading, or you are about to quote the PROFILE line as the command cost. HOW: run wkappbot skill read pulsestep-force-mode-ring-trail for the Mark-versus-Line contract and the silent-trace rule, then measure by running the STAGING exe directly with WKAPPBOT_PROFILE set to 1 -- never through the launcher, which adds its own pipe wait. WHY: measured 2026-09-06 on wktest-core-manual-v7.9.197 invoked directly. --version totalled 164ms with NO checkpoint firing, so core startup is thin and spread rather than one slow step. skill read totalled 908ms with dispatch-returned at +744ms and memory +166MB. skill --help totalled 1348ms with help-printed at +1266ms and memory +376MB -- so printing STATIC HELP TEXT costs more than reading the whole skill catalog, and both allocate hundreds of megabytes inside dispatch. Neither cold start nor the catalog explains that. AND THE OLD INSTRUMENT LIES: the same 1348ms run printed PROFILE 25ms command=skill, so that line does not measure command cost; a sector concluded from it that only 20-22ms of a 2173ms invocation was movable, and that is retracted -- over a second is movable.
